meta.notes: CRITICAL FINDING: The dataset contains ZERO bechina edges for reference === 110. The bechina subgraph is completely empty. All packages below are derived exclusively from the source text gap analysis (Step 5), identifying explicit bechina language in the six-line Torah. The teaching opens with the verse 'Lo yamush sefer haTorah hazeh mipicha' (Joshua 1:8) and builds a tight binary between Torah as pure spirituality (ruchaniyut) — which, being spiritual, takes no space and can be retained fully — and Torah materialized (mamashut/gashmiyut) — which, becoming physical, is subject to spatial limits and generates forgetting. Two packages emerge with a clean good/evil mirror structure: Package 1 (Torah = Ruchaniyut = Sekhel Ruchani = Lo Tofes Makom) and Package 2 (Mamashut = Gashmiyut = Yamush as linguistic root). Forgetting (shikhah) and retention (kiyum halimud) are identified as eitza consequences, not bechina nodes, based on the explicit eitza marker 'u'mizeh BA hashikhah' (from this COMES forgetting). The Rav Yosef story at the end of the Torah serves as illustrative proof, not new bechina content — it recaps the same teaching using the verse 'lo yamushu vi'yegushmu' as a mnemonic for ruchaniyut → kiyum.

packages.label: תּוֹרָה וְרוּחָנִיּוּת
packages.reason: This cluster represents the positive pole of Torah #110. The Rebbe opens with a definitional identity: 'הַתּוֹרָה הִיא רוּחָנִיּוּת' — Torah IS spirituality. The bechina marker 'הִיא' (IS) is the strongest possible identification in Hebrew — Torah and ruchaniyut are the same essential reality viewed from different angles. From this identity flows the next bechina: 'דָּבָר רוּחָנִי אֵינוֹ תּוֹפֵס מָקוֹם' — a spiritual thing takes no space. The phrase 'eino tofes makom' is not a consequence of ruchaniyut but a DEFINITION of it — what it means to be spiritual IS to be without spatial limit. The 'lo tofes makom' quality is therefore a bechina of ruchaniyut, not an eitza from it. The third node is 'sekhel ruchani' — the spiritual intellect of the person whose 'sikhlо ruchani' (intellect is spiritual). The teaching establishes that this person's sekhel shares the same essential nature as Torah's spirituality: 'yakhol litpos kol haTorah kulah ve-lo yishkach davar' — because the vessel (sekhel) and the content (Torah) are the same spiritual nature, they can coexist without displacement. The dominant node is Torah (תּוֹרָה) because it is named in the opening verse and is the hub connecting both ruchaniyut and sekhel ruchani through the identity relationship. The entire teaching circles back to Torah: at the end (line 6), the Rav Yosef story concludes 'ki lo yihyeh shikhah, ki davar ruchani eino tofes makom' — restating the Torah-Ruchaniyut-Lo Tofes Makom triple identity as the reason learning endures.

source_bechinot.bechina_marker: definitional identity — to be spiritual IS to take no space; repeated twice (lines 2 and 6) as the teaching's axiom

source_bechinot.source_quote: וַאֲשֶׁר זַךְ יָשָׁר פָּעֳלוֹ, וְשִׂכְלוֹ רוּחָנִי, יָכוֹל לִתְפֹּס כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ
source_bechinot.bechina_marker: parallel nature — the spiritual sekhel can hold all of Torah because both share the same ruchani essence; a physical vessel cannot hold a spiritual content unlimited, but a spiritual vessel can

packages.label: מַמָּשׁוּת וְגַשְׁמִיּוּת
packages.reason: This cluster represents the negative pole of Torah #110 — the evil/deficiency mirror of Package 1. The Rebbe explicitly equates mamashut (substance/materiality) and gashmiyut (physicality) throughout the teaching, using them interchangeably in two parallel formulations: 'mamashut ve-gashmiyut be-divrei haTorah' (line 4) and 'mamashut ve-gashmiyut' (line 5). This repeated coupling is the Rebbe's own declaration that these are two expressions of the same essential nature — the antithesis of ruchaniyut. The third node is the word 'yamush' itself, which the Rebbe explicitly derives from the root of mamashut: 'yamush — mileshon mamashut' (yamush IS from the language of mamashut). This is a classic bechina move: deriving the essential nature of a biblical term from its etymological root, establishing that 'yamush' (departing from the mouth) IS mamashut (materialization). The bechina marker 'mileshon' (from the language of) functions identically to 'bechina' — it identifies the conceptual essence embedded in the word's form. The dominant node is mamashut (מַמָּשׁוּת) because it is the most frequently mentioned concept (appears 5 times across lines 3-6), it is the etymological source of 'yamush', and it is explicitly paired with gashmiyut as the negative counterforce to Torah's ruchaniyut. The good/evil mirror is perfect: Torah = ruchaniyut = spiritual sekhel = lo tofes makom (Package 1) vs. materialized Torah = mamashut = gashmiyut = yamush (Package 2).

source_bechinot.bechina_marker: repeated coupling in two parallel formulations (lines 4 and 5) — the Rebbe uses them as synonyms, establishing shared essential nature

source_bechinot.source_quote: יָמוּשׁ – מִלְּשׁוֹן מַמָּשׁוּת. כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: וְיָמֵשׁ חֹשֶׁךְ
source_bechinot.bechina_marker: מִלְּשׁוֹן (from the language/root of) — etymological bechina: yamush IS from mamashut, identifying the word's essential conceptual nature

good_evil_mirror_structure.description: Torah #110 has a clean binary good/evil mirror. Package 1 (Torah/Ruchaniyut) is the exact positive counterpart of Package 2 (Mamashut/Gashmiyut). The same Torah-text can be either: (a) held spiritually — then it IS ruchaniyut, IS sekhel ruchani, IS lo tofes makom, IS unlimited and unforgettable; or (b) materialized — then it IS mamashut, IS gashmiyut, IS yamush (departed/materialized), IS bounded and forgotten. The two packages are the two possible orientations of the same Torah toward the same intellect. The practical instruction (eitza) between packages: 'hizaher shelo tihyeh mamashut ve-gashmiyut be-divrei haTorah' — be careful that Torah should not become materialized. This eitza connects Package 2 (danger) to Package 1 (goal). Forgetting (shikhah) is the eitza consequence of Package 2; retention/kiyum is the eitza consequence of Package 1.

eitza_nodes_excluded.reason: Forgetting is explicitly introduced with the eitza marker 'u'mizeh BA hashikhah' — from materialization COMES (ba) forgetting. The word 'ba' (comes) marks causal flow, not parallel nature. Forgetting is not a bechina of mamashut but an eitza consequence of it. Excluded from packages.

The sustaining of learning ('yitkayem talmmudo') is the positive eitza result when Torah remains spiritual: 'shelo yamushu vi'yegushmu mipicha, va'azai yitkayem talmmudo'. The 'va'azai' (and then) is classic eitza language — this is the benefit that FLOWS from ruchaniyut, not a parallel aspect of it. Excluded from packages.

Measure and limit: 'yesh lah shiyur ve-kitzba' — mamashut GIVES Torah a shiyur ve-kitzba. This is a property that flows FROM mamashut (eitza from Package 2), not a bechina equivalent of it. The 'yesh lah' phrasing indicates attribution/consequence, not identity. Excluded from packages.

The Rebbe cites the darkness of Egypt ('vayamesh choshekh' — Exodus 10:21) only as a linguistic proof that 'yamush' derives from 'mamashut' (the darkness that could be touched/felt). The darkness itself is not a bechina node in this Torah — it is a scriptural proof-text for the etymological bechina, not a new conceptual element. Excluded from packages.

This Torah requires full bechina edge extraction before it can be represented in the graph. The teaching is structurally simple: 6 lines, one binary opposition (ruchaniyut vs. mamashut), 7 nodes total (4 good, 3 evil), 5 bechina pairs, 3 eitza nodes excluded.
